question: q-129662

original_content.knowledge_point: Determining a Valid Region to Define a Double Integral Over a Non-Rectangular Domain
original_content.problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}9-{x}^{2}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}(9-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-3,3]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[-4,4]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[-3,3]\times [0,2]$
original_content.worked_solution:
First, let's draw our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14053940/assets/4a8671db243a19fb258f6144d6aba1b193e237ef93d45d877829f80b93bc7d36.png)

Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}9-{x}^{2}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}(9-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangle III does not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangles I and II cover the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

corrected_content.problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}9-{x}^{2}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}(9-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

Require $D\subseteq R$, so the rectangle contains the entire region. Which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-3,3]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[-4,4]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[-3,3]\times [0,2]$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The ellipse $x^2/9+y^2\le1$ has horizontal extent $[-3,3]$ and vertical extent $[-1,1]$. Rectangles I and II both contain this entire bounding box and thus all of $D$. Rectangle III excludes $(0,-1)$, so it does not contain all of $D$.

On either containing rectangle, $f=9-x^2$ on $D$ and zero on $R\setminus D$. Consequently $\iint_R f\,dA=\iint_D(9-x^2)\,dA$. The answer is "I and II only".
